knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With Many Zeros

question.:question/problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 3 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $D=\det(A)$.

Expand $D$ along column 1; only 2 nonzero entries contribute.

$$
\begin{aligned}D &=(-2)(-1)^{1+1}\begin{vmatrix}2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\ &\quad +(-1)(-1)^{4+1}\begin{vmatrix}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 3\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Write $D_{1}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 1 and column 1, and $D_{2}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 4 and column 1.

Expand $D_{1}$ along row 3; only 1 nonzero entry contributes.

$$
D_{1}=(3)(-1)^{3+2}\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 0 & 3\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Write $D_{11}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 3 and column 2.

Evaluate the two by two determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{11} &=\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 0 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\ &=(2)(3)-(3)(0) \\ &=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these minor values,

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{1} &=(3)(-1)^{3+2}(6) \\ &=-18.\end{aligned}
$$

Expand $D_{2}$ along column 2; only 1 nonzero entry contributes.

$$
D_{2}=(-1)(-1)^{3+2}\begin{vmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 2 & 3\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Write $D_{21}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 3 and column 2.

Evaluate the two by two determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{21} &=\begin{vmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 2 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\ &=(2)(3)-(0)(2) \\ &=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these minor values,

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{2} &=(-1)(-1)^{3+2}(6) \\ &=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these minor values,

$$
\begin{aligned}D &=(-2)(-1)^{1+1}(-18)+(-1)(-1)^{4+1}(6) \\ &=42.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\det(A)=42$.

knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With Many Zeros

question.:question/problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -2\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $D=\det(A)$.

Expand $D$ along row 4; only 2 nonzero entries contribute.

$$
\begin{aligned}D &=(2)(-1)^{4+2}\begin{vmatrix}-3 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{vmatrix} \\ &\quad +(-2)(-1)^{4+4}\begin{vmatrix}-3 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Write $D_{1}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 4 and column 2, and $D_{2}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 4 and column 4.

The matrix in $D_{1}$ is triangular, so multiply its diagonal entries.

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{1} &=\begin{vmatrix}-3 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{vmatrix} \\ &=(-3)\cdot(-2)\cdot(-2) \\ &=-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Expand $D_{2}$ along column 2; only 1 nonzero entry contributes.

$$
D_{2}=(1)(-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix}-2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Write $D_{21}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 1 and column 2.

Evaluate the two by two determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{21} &=\begin{vmatrix}-2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=(-2)(1)-(-2)(0) \\ &=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these minor values,

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{2} &=(1)(-1)^{1+2}(-2) \\ &=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these minor values,

$$
\begin{aligned}D &=(2)(-1)^{4+2}(-12)+(-2)(-1)^{4+4}(2) \\ &=-28.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\det(A)=-28$.

knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With Many Zeros

question.:question/problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $D=\det(A)$.

Expand $D$ along row 1; only 2 nonzero entries contribute.

$$
\begin{aligned}D &=(-2)(-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix}-1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\ &\quad +(1)(-1)^{1+3}\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 3\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Write $D_{1}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 1 and column 2, and $D_{2}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 1 and column 3.

Expand $D_{1}$ along column 2; only 1 nonzero entry contributes.

$$
D_{1}=(-1)(-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix}0 & -1 \\ 3 & 3\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Write $D_{11}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 1 and column 2.

Evaluate the two by two determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{11} &=\begin{vmatrix}0 & -1 \\ 3 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\ &=(0)(3)-(-1)(3) \\ &=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these minor values,

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{1} &=(-1)(-1)^{1+2}(3) \\ &=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Expand $D_{2}$ along column 2; only 1 nonzero entry contributes.

$$
D_{2}=(2)(-1)^{2+2}\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 3 & 3\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Write $D_{21}$ for the minor obtained by deleting row 2 and column 2.

Evaluate the two by two determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{21} &=\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 3 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\ &=(-1)(3)-(0)(3) \\ &=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these minor values,

$$
\begin{aligned}D_{2} &=(2)(-1)^{2+2}(-3) \\ &=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these minor values,

$$
\begin{aligned}D &=(-2)(-1)^{1+2}(3)+(1)(-1)^{1+3}(-6) \\ &=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\det(A)=0$.
